turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hey Maya, ready for your Quillbase mock? I'm stepping into the hiring manager role now. Could you share an example of a project where you took raw numbers and solved an operational problem?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, definitely. Back during my graduate program, the university library had zero visibility into room usage. I created a Tableau dashboard tracking study room reservations, and the campus library still relies on it today to manage bookings.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That shows real initiative. How would you apply that same analytical habit to building an outbound territory for Quillbase?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Well, in SaaS sales, you can't just blindly dial down a list. I'd look at account engagement and intent signals the same way, prioritizing accounts that show real activity so I'm not wasting time on cold leads.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That makes sense. That covers what I wanted to ask, so do you have any questions for me about the team or the role?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Um, nope, honestly you covered everything I was wondering about. I think I'm good on my end!

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Stepping out of the interviewer role now. How did that feel from your side?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It felt pretty comfortable, honestly. I think the dashboard example came out a lot smoother than my stories usually do.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Your dashboard story landed really well. But you completely skipped asking me anything when I opened the floor at the end. What happened there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, you caught me. Whenever an interview wraps up, I always completely forget to ask questions of my own. I get so relieved to be done talking that my mind just blanks out.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Leaving without questions can make you seem uninterested. What if you kept two questions written on a sticky note right in front of you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, having a sticky note right on my monitor would keep me from spacing out. What kind of question works best for a BDR screen?

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Ask what distinguishes their top rep from the rest of the team. How does that one feel to say out loud?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I like that a lot. What distinguishes your top-performing BDR from everyone else? It feels sharp and shows I care about hitting quota.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That sounded crisp and natural. Do you want to run the ending one more time to lock it in?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, let's do a quick reset on the ending, just so I nail it.
